sections.title: Habit and desert habitat
sections.text: Cylindropuntia bigelovii, teddy-bear cholla, is a shrubby cactus of the Sonoran and Mojave deserts. It reaches about 1.5 m. Its cylindrical segments detach easily and are densely covered in pale spines, often giving the plant a woolly appearance.

sections.title: Flowers and spines
sections.text: Its greenish-yellow flowers appear in spring; the spines and glochids readily attach to skin or clothing. The plate accurately shows the dense spiny appearance, segments and flower. No reliable food use was included.
